quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When you take alcohol and drugs together, the effects:

options.text: Are less dangerous than taking either one alone.
Can be stronger than taking either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than taking either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it unsafe to ride. Combining drugs with alcohol makes them even more dangerous.

questions.question: The best way to handle someone tailgating you is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgaters is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things more dangerous because they will keep tailgating at the higher speed.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is just part of riding a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise can cause permanent hearing loss. Ear protection while riding can protect your hearing and still let you hear important sounds like sirens or car horns.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. Services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to weave when riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get over the surface faster.
Zigzag to get the attention of other drivers.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across the grooves or gratings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across the grooves or gratings.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves when riding over grooves or gratings, stay at a steady speed and go straight across. Trying to zigzag to stay in your lane is more dangerous.

questions.question: The best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle ride is to:
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long rides, limit your riding time each day and take frequent rest breaks. Avoid artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue can happen when they wear off.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: All keep a safe distance between each other.
Follow as closely as possible to each other.
Not worry about distances between riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: All keep a safe distance between each other.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This lets riders stay close together while keeping safe distances between each other.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the roadway is divided ahead.

questions.question: If a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast, they may:

options.text: Have better control of their motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Taking a turn or curve too fast causes a rider to lose control. The motorcycle may cross into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: What should be your first concern when buying a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: How well it protects your head

questions.correctAnswerText: How well it protects your head
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet for protection first. Pick one that fastens securely, fits well, and is DOT-compliant.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, you should:

options.text: Keep riding because the danger has passed.
Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop to remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: Pull off the road after riding over an object. Check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is caught in the drive chain or belt before continuing.

questions.question: When traveling at night, judging distances is:

options.text: About the same as during the day.

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances at night than during the day. Shadows and light help you see distance during the day. At night, artificial lighting may distort or remove these helpful clues.

questions.question: When a tailgater is following you closely, you should:
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. If you speed up, they may just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of the lane helps a car driver see you in their side mirror. What is a problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
Wind may prevent the use of a side mirror.
Motorists should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: No matter which helmet style you choose, you get the most protection when your helmet:
questions.explanation: You get the most protection from your helmet when it meets DOT and state standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Be loose so the wind can catch the fabric.
Fit snug enough that they don't flap in the wind.
Be so tight that you cannot move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snug enough that they don't flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snug enough that they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: There is less grip available for braking when:

options.text: A motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle is leaning, such as in a turn, there is less grip available for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: The risk of head or neck injury is reduced:
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries can happen at any speed when riding a motorcycle. A quality helmet worn properly greatly reduces the risk of these injuries.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, signal your intentions, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, identify hazards, and be ready for changing conditions.

questions.question: A person riding a motorcycle:

options.text: May carry a small package in one hand.
May carry a package with their hands if it does not block their view.
May not carry a package with their hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not carry a package with their hands.
questions.explanation: In Alabama, you cannot operate a motorcycle while carrying anything. You must keep both hands on the handlebars at all times.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Look straight ahead in front of the motorcycle.
Not be willing to move to avoid a hazard.
Look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds down the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds down the road.
questions.explanation: Look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds on the road to reduce collision risk. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: Which color should you wear to increase your visibility when riding during the day?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothes even in daylight.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may proceed through the intersection with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait for a green signal before turning in that direction.

questions.question: You should pick a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you most visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
You like, without thinking about other drivers.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you most visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you and where you have space around your motorcycle. Change your position as road conditions change. No single lane position is always best or worst.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Are easily seen by other drivers.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which material provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather or sturdy synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen in daylight, you:

options.text: Do not need to wear bright colors during the day.
Should wear bright colors during the day.
Should wear dark colors during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear bright colors during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright colors when riding to make yourself more visible, even during the day.

questions.question: You approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle starts moving.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space and go slowly. Be ready to stop at any time.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed.
